record.nameMeaning: "Double beam", for the double-beamed chevron bones under its tail
record.oneLiner: An enormous long-necked, whip-tailed diplodocid sauropod.
record.description: Diplodocus was a very large, long-necked, quadrupedal sauropod with a long, whip-like tail and a largely horizontal posture. D. carnegii is one of the longest dinosaurs known from a complete skeleton, at 24–26 m. It lived in the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of western North America, where its great size may have deterred predators like Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus.

discovery.who: S. W. Williston (found); named by O. C. Marsh, 1878

notableFacts.text: One of the longest dinosaurs known from a complete skeleton (24–26 m).
Named "double beam" after the double-beamed chevron bones under its whip-like tail.
No skull can be confidently assigned to Diplodocus itself.
